group_metadata.title: Empires of Ancient India: Dynastic Atlases, Battles & Inscriptions
group_metadata.subtitle: Geospatial Evolution of Sovereignty from the 16 Mahajanapadas to the Classical Golden Ages (600 BCE – 850 CE)
group_metadata.description: Interactive geospatial atlases mapping shifting imperial frontiers, decisive battlefields, and epigraphic records in Ashokan Brahmi, Classical Sanskrit, Ancient Greek, and Sangam Tamil. Verified from Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) Memoirs, Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum (CII), and peer-reviewed historical corpora.
group_metadata.special_mention: Alexander the Great's Campaign & Macedonian Limit (326 BCE)

empires.name: 16 Mahajanapadas & Early Republics
empires.era_type: Iron Age Second Urbanisation & Emergence of States

capitals.name: Rajagriha (Magadha)
capitals.role: Ancient Magadhan capital encircled by cyclopean stone walls

capitals.name: Shravasti (Kosala)
capitals.role: Commercial hub of the Rapti river and seat of King Prasenajit

capitals.name: Kaushambi (Vatsa)
capitals.role: Yamuna river trade nexus ruled by King Udayana

capitals.name: Ujjayini (Avanti)
capitals.role: Western trade junction on the Dakshinapatha highway

capitals.name: Taxila (Gandhara)
capitals.role: Foremost pan-Asian Vedic university and northern trade crossroad

capitals.name: Vaishali (Vajji)
capitals.role: Metropolis of the Licchavi republic, the world's earliest recorded confederacy

boundary_phases.description: Independent co-existence of monarchies (Kosala, Magadha, Vatsa, Avanti) and oligarchic ganas (Vajji, Malla, Koliya, Shakya) across the Gangetic drainage.

boundary_phases.phase: Magadhan Expansion under Bimbisara & Ajatashatru (c. 490 BCE)
boundary_phases.description: Annexation of Anga (Champa) by Bimbisara and the 16-year war of Ajatashatru against the Vajji Confederacy using the Mahashilakantaka catapult and Rathamusala scythed chariot.

battles.name: Magadha–Vajji War
battles.parties: Ajatashatru of Magadha vs. Licchavi / Vajji Confederacy
battles.summary: Ajatashatru deployed two groundbreaking military innovations: the Mahashilakantaka (heavy stone siege catapult) and the Rathamusala (chariot with revolving scythe blades). Ended the independence of Vaishali.
battles.source: Buddhist Digha Nikaya & Jaina Bhagavati Sutra

events.title: Birth of Gautama Buddha in Lumbini (Shakya Republic)
Bimbisara establishes Haryanka Dynasty in Magadha
First Buddhist Council convened at Rajagriha under Ajatashatru

shloka_epigraph.text: अङ्गा मगधा च कासी च कोसलो वज्जी मल्ला चेती वंसा कुरु पञ्चाला मच्छ सुरसेना अस्सको अवन्ती गन्धारा कम्बोचा ति सोळस महाजनपदा।
shloka_epigraph.translation: These are the sixteen great realms: Anga, Magadha, Kasi, Kosala, Vajji, Malla, Ceti, Vamsa, Kuru, Pancala, Maccha, Surasena, Assaka, Avanti, Gandhara, and Kamboja.

empires.historical_map_title: The Sixteen Mahājanapadas — India's First Republics & Kingdoms (c. 600–345 BCE)

empires.name: Magadha Ascendancy: Haryanka, Shishunaga & Nanda

capitals.name: Pataliputra (Patna)
capitals.role: Founded by Udayin at the confluence of Ganga and Son; fortified imperial capital

boundary_phases.phase: Mahapadma Nanda's Pan-North Indian Zenith (c. 340 BCE)
boundary_phases.description: Mahapadma Nanda assumed the title 'Ekarat' (Sole Sovereign). His domain stretched from the Beas River in Punjab to the Bengal delta, and south to the Vindhya mountains and Godavari valley.

battles.name: Conquest of the Kshatriya Dynasties
battles.parties: Mahapadma Nanda vs. Ikshvakus, Panchalas, Kasis, Haihayas, Kalingas, Asmakas, Kurus, Maithilas
battles.summary: Mahapadma earned the epithets 'Sarva-Kshatrantaka' (Destroyer of all Kshatriyas) and 'Bhargava' (like Parashurama) in the Puranas for systematically subduing traditional oligarchies.
battles.source: Matsya Purana & Vayu Purana Dynastic Chronicles

events.title: Shishunaga establishes dynasty, destroys ancient rival kingdom of Avanti
Mahapadma Nanda founds the Nanda dynasty and establishes regular treasury taxation
Greek historians note Dhana Nanda's standing army of 200,000 infantry, 20,000 cavalry, 2,000 chariots, 4,000 war elephants

shloka_epigraph.text: महापद्मपतिः कश्चित् नन्दः क्षत्रविनाशकृत् । ततो नृपा भविष्यन्ति शूद्रप्रायास्त्वधार्मिकाः ॥ एकराट् स महापद्मो ह्येकच्छत्रो भविष्यति ।
shloka_epigraph.translation: Mahapadma Nanda will arise, the destroyer of all Kshatriyas. He will be the sole sovereign (Ekarat) ruling under a single imperial parasol (Eka-chhatra).

sources.title: The Age of the Nandas and Mauryas
sources.author: K.A. Nilakanta Sastri

empires.historical_map_title: The Later Vedic Age — Janapadas of the Gangetic Plain (c. 1100–600 BCE)

empires.name: Alexander the Great: Trans-Continental Empire & Indian Frontier

capitals.name: Pella (Macedonia)
capitals.role: Macedonian royal birthplace of Alexander and launchpad of the Pan-Hellenic expedition

capitals.name: Alexandria (Egypt)
capitals.role: Mediterranean metropolis founded 331 BCE; tomb of Alexander and Ptolemaic capital

capitals.name: Babylon (Mesopotamia)
capitals.role: Administrative center of Alexander's world empire where he died in June 323 BCE

boundary_phases.phase: Macedonian Empire at its Greatest Extent (323 BCE)
boundary_phases.description: Alexander's unbroken trans-continental empire stretched 5,000 km from the Adriatic Sea and the Nile Valley, through Anatolia, Mesopotamia, and Persia, into Bactria, Gandhara, and the Indus River.

battles.name: Battle of the Granicus
battles.parties: Alexander III vs. Persian Satraps & Greek Mercenaries
battles.summary: First major victory in Asia Minor. Alexander personally led the Companion Cavalry charge across the river.

battles.name: Battle of Issus
battles.parties: Alexander III vs. Darius III of Persia
battles.summary: Decisive tactical triumph at the Pinarus river; Darius fled leaving his royal family and imperial chariot behind.

battles.name: Battle of Gaugamela
battles.parties: Alexander III vs. Darius III & Royal Persian Host
battles.summary: Masterstroke wedge charge broke the Persian center. Alexander crowned 'Lord of Asia' and captured Babylon, Susa, and Persepolis.
battles.source: Arrian III.8–15 & Plutarch, Life of Alexander 31–33

battles.name: Battle of the Hydaspes (Jhelum)
battles.summary: Night river-crossing under torrential monsoon storms. Alexander outflanked Porus's 200 war elephants. Alexander was so impressed by Porus's courage that he reinstated him as a client king and expanded his realm.
battles.source: Arrian V.9–19 & Quintus Curtius Rufus VIII.13–14

battles.name: Mutiny at the Hyphasis (Beas River)
battles.summary: Exhausted by 8 years of marching, terrified by reports of the Nanda Empire's 4,000 war elephants, Coenus spoke for the troops: 'If there is one thing above all which a successful man should know, it is when to say: Hold, enough.' Alexander erected 12 monumental altars to the Olympian gods and turned south down the Indus.

events.title: Alexander crosses the Hellespont into Asia with 32,000 infantry and 5,100 cavalry
Foundation of Alexandria in Egypt and pilgrimage to the Oracle of Amun at Siwa
Siege of the Rock of Aornos on the Indus; submission of Taxila
Descent down the Indus; Nearchus commands the fleet across the Persian Gulf while Alexander marches through the Gedrosian Desert
Death of Alexander at Babylon at age 32; partition of the empire among the Diadochi generals

shloka_epigraph.text:
«Ὦ παῖ, ζήτει σεαυτῷ βασιλείαν ἴσην· Μακεδονία γάρ σε οὐ χωρεῖ.»
«Ἀλέξανδρος ὁ Φιλίππου ὧδε κατέπαυσε τὸν δρόμον.»
shloka_epigraph.translation:
"O my son, seek a kingdom worthy of thyself; for Macedonia cannot contain thee." — Philip II to Alexander upon taming Bucephalus.
"Alexander son of Philip here called a halt to his course." — Inscription erected at the 12 Altars of the Hyphasis (Beas River).
shloka_epigraph.citation: Plutarch, Life of Alexander 6.5 & Arrian, Anabasis of Alexander V.29
shloka_epigraph.verified_from: Loeb Classical Library, Harvard University Press

sources.title: Alexander the Great in the Punjab
sources.author: Buddha Prakash

empires.historical_map_title: After the Mauryas — Shungas, Greeks and Sakas (c. 185 BCE–50 CE)

empires.name: Mauryan Empire & Pan-Indian Hegemony
empires.era_type: Largest Unified Empire in South Asian History
empires.religion: Buddhism (under Ashoka), Jainism (under Chandragupta) & Vedic Dharma

capitals.name: Pataliputra
capitals.role: Imperial seat described by Megasthenes: 64 gates, 570 towers, 9 miles long along the Ganga

capitals.name: Taxila (Uttarapatha)
capitals.role: Northern viceroyalty governing the Hellenistic frontier satrapies

capitals.name: Ujjayini (Avantiratha)
capitals.role: Western viceroyalty overseeing trade with Barygaza and Arabia

capitals.name: Tosali (Kalinga)
capitals.role: Eastern viceroyalty established following the Kalinga War

capitals.name: Suvarnagiri (Dakshinapatha)
capitals.role: Southern viceroyalty in Karnataka governing goldfields and Deccan provinces

boundary_phases.phase: Chandragupta's Foundation & Treaty with Seleucus (303 BCE)
boundary_phases.description: Treaty of 303 BCE between Chandragupta Maurya and Seleucus I Nicator: Mauryan sovereignty recognized over Arachosia (Kandahar), Paropamisadae (Kabul), Gedrosia (Balochistan), and Aria (Herat) in exchange for 500 war elephants.

boundary_phases.phase: Ashoka the Great's Peak Pan-Indian Empire (c. 250 BCE)
boundary_phases.description: Zenith covering ~5 million square kilometres. Extends from the Hindu Kush to the Pennar River in southern Karnataka, marked by Ashoka's Major Rock Edicts from Kandahar to Brahmagiri.

battles.name: Mauryan–Seleucid War
battles.parties: Chandragupta Maurya vs. Seleucus I Nicator
battles.summary: Chandragupta halted Seleucus's advance across the Indus. The peace treaty ceded all four eastern satrapies of the former Achaemenid empire to the Mauryans, established marriage alliance (epigamia), and sent Megasthenes as ambassador to Pataliputra.
battles.source: Appian, Roman History: The Syrian Wars 55 & Strabo, Geographica XV.2.9

battles.name: Kalinga War
battles.parties: Ashoka the Great vs. State of Kalinga
battles.summary: 100,000 slain, 150,000 deported, and hundreds of thousands perished from starvation. The profound remorse inspired Ashoka to renounce military conquest (Dig-Vijaya) and adopt conquest by moral law (Dharma-Vijaya).
battles.source: Ashoka's Major Rock Edict XIII (Shahbazgarhi & Kalsi texts)

events.title: Chandragupta Maurya and Chanakya overthrow Dhana Nanda, founding the Mauryan Empire
Megasthenes authors 'Indica', detailing civic administration, castes, and Mauryan courts
Coronation of Ashoka (Devanampiya Piyadasi) as third Mauryan Emperor
Third Buddhist Council convened at Pataliputra under Moggaliputta Tissa; Buddhist missions dispatched to Greece, Egypt, Sri Lanka, and Burma

shloka_epigraph.text: 𑀤𑁂𑀯𑀸𑀦𑀁𑀧𑀺𑀬𑁂𑀦 𑀧𑀺𑀬𑀤𑀲𑀺𑀦𑀸 𑀭𑀸𑀜𑀸 𑀯𑀻𑀲𑀢𑀺𑀯𑀲𑀸𑀪𑀺𑀲𑀺𑀢𑁂𑀦 𑀅𑀢𑀦 𑀆𑀕𑀸𑀘𑁆𑀘 𑀫𑀳𑀻𑀬𑀺𑀢𑁂 𑀳𑀺𑀤 𑀩𑀼𑀥𑁂 𑀚𑀸𑀢𑁂 𑀲𑀓𑁆𑀬𑀫𑀼𑀦𑀻𑀢𑀺 ॥
shloka_epigraph.translation: "King Devanampiya Piyadasi, when he had been consecrated twenty years, came here in person and worshipped, because here was born the Buddha, the Sage of the Shakyas. He caused a stone pillar to be erected and exempted the village of Lumbini from taxes."
shloka_epigraph.verified_from: Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum (CII), Vol. I: Inscriptions of Asoka (E. Hultzsch, 1925, p. 164)

sources.title: Asoka and the Decline of the Mauryas
sources.author: Romila Thapar

sources.title: Inscriptions of Asoka
sources.author: E. Hultzsch
sources.publisher: Archaeological Survey of India (CII Vol. I)

empires.historical_map_title: The First Empire — India under the Mauryas (c. 322–185 BCE)

empires.name: Post-Mauryan & Indo-Greek Kingdoms

capitals.name: Sagala (Sialkot)
capitals.role: Indo-Greek capital celebrated in the Milinda Panha as a splendid commercial hub

capitals.name: Vidisha (Besnagar)
capitals.role: Shunga secondary capital; location of the famous Heliodorus Garuda pillar

capitals.name: Pataliputra
capitals.role: Seat of Pushyamitra Shunga following the regicide of Brihadratha

boundary_phases.phase: Menander I's Peak Indo-Greek Realm (c. 150 BCE)
boundary_phases.description: Menander I (Milinda) ruled from the Paropamisadae and Arachosia across the Punjab to the Yamuna, striking refined bilingual silver drachms bearing Greek and Kharosthi inscriptions.

boundary_phases.phase: Shunga Empire in Central & Eastern India (c. 175 BCE)
boundary_phases.description: Pushyamitra Shunga revived Vedic Ashvamedha sacrifices and patronized the reconstruction of the Sanchi Stupa gateways and Bharhut balustrades.

battles.name: Battle of the Sindhu River (Vasumitra vs. Greeks)
battles.parties: Prince Vasumitra (Shunga) vs. Indo-Greek Yavana Cavalry
battles.summary: Vasumitra guarded Pushyamitra's sacrificial horse and defeated an encroaching Yavana force on the banks of the Sindhu (Indus or Kali Sindh in Madhya Pradesh).

events.title: Pushyamitra Shunga assassinates Brihadratha Maurya, establishing Shunga Dynasty
Accession of Menander I (Milinda); dialogues with Buddhist sage Nagasena recorded in Milinda Panha
Heliodorus, Greek ambassador from King Antialcidas of Taxila, erects Garuda pillar at Vidisha

shloka_epigraph.text: 𑀤𑁂𑀯𑀤𑁂𑀯𑀲 𑀯𑀸𑀲𑀼𑀤𑁂𑀯𑀲 𑀕𑀭𑀼𑀟𑀥𑁆𑀯𑀚𑁄 𑀅𑀬𑀁 𑀓𑀸𑀭𑀺𑀢𑁄 𑀇𑀬 𑀳𑁂𑀮𑀺𑀑𑀤𑁄𑀭𑁂𑀡 𑀪𑀸𑀕𑀯𑀢𑁂𑀦... 𑀢𑁆𑀭𑀻𑀦𑀺 𑀅𑀫𑀼𑀢𑀧𑀤𑀸𑀦𑀺 𑀲𑀼𑀅𑀦𑀼𑀞𑀺𑀢𑀸𑀦𑀺 𑀦𑀬𑀁𑀢𑀺 𑀲𑀕𑀁 — 𑀤𑀫𑁄 𑀘𑀸𑀕𑁄 𑀅𑀧𑁆𑀭𑀫𑀸𑀤𑁄 ॥
shloka_epigraph.translation: "This Garuda column of Vasudeva, the God of gods, was erected here by Heliodorus, a Bhagavata, son of Dion and inhabitant of Taxila, who came as Greek ambassador from King Antialcidas to King Bhagabhadra... Three are the immortal steps which lead to heaven when well observed: Self-restraint (Dama), Renunciation (Tyaga), and Vigilance (Apramada)."
shloka_epigraph.verified_from: Archaeological Survey of India, Annual Report 1908–1909, pp. 126–129

empires.historical_map_title: After the Mauryas — Shungas, Greeks and Sakas (c. 185 BCE–50 CE)

empires.name: Satavahana Empire & Deccan Maritime Ascendancy
empires.era_type: Deccan Bridge & Indian Ocean Seaborne Trade
empires.religion: Brahmanical Hinduism (Vedic Yagnas) & Buddhist Stupa Patronage

capitals.name: Pratishthana (Paithan)
capitals.role: Western capital on the Godavari controlling Western Ghats pass trade to Sopara and Kalyan

capitals.name: Amaravati / Dharanikota
capitals.role: Eastern capital on the Krishna; site of the great Mahachaitya marble stupa

boundary_phases.description: Gautamiputra defeated the Western Kshatrapa ruler Nahapana, restruck over 13,000 Kshatrapa silver coins (Jogalthambi hoard), and restored Satavahana supremacy over Gujarat, Malwa, Maharashtra, and Andhra.

battles.name: Battle of Govardhana (Overthrow of Nahapana)
battles.parties: Gautamiputra Satakarni vs. Nahapana of Western Kshatrapas
battles.summary: Decisive victory annihilating the Kshaharata dynasty. Gautamiputra annexed Aparanta (Konkan), Saurashtra, Kukura, and Anupa.
battles.source: Nasik Cave 3 Inscription of Queen Mother Gautami Balashri

events.title: Simuka establishes Satavahana rule in the Deccan
Traditional inauguration of the Shalivahana Shaka calendar era
Yajna Sri Satakarni issues ship-motif silver coins celebrating trans-oceanic Indian Ocean trade

shloka_epigraph.text: 𑀭𑀸𑀜𑁄 𑀕𑁄𑀢𑀫𑀻𑀧𑀼𑀢𑀲 𑀲𑀸𑀢𑀓𑀡𑀺𑀲... 𑀔𑀔𑀭𑀸𑀢𑀯𑀲𑀦𑀺𑀭𑁆𑀯𑀲𑁂𑀲𑀓𑀭𑀲 𑀲𑀸𑀢𑀯𑀸𑀳𑀦𑀓𑀼𑀮𑀬𑀲𑀧𑀢𑀺𑀞𑀸𑀧𑀦𑀓𑀭𑀲 𑀢𑁆𑀭𑀺𑀲𑀫𑀼𑀤𑁆𑀭𑀢𑁄𑀬𑀧𑀻𑀢𑀯𑀸𑀳𑀦𑀲 ॥
shloka_epigraph.translation: "Of King Gautamiputra Satakarni... who destroyed the pride and arrogance of the Kshatriyas, who completely eradicated the Kshaharata lineage, who restored the glory of the Satavahana dynasty, whose chargers drank the waters of the three oceans (Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea, and Indian Ocean)."
shloka_epigraph.verified_from: Epigraphia Indica, Vol. VIII, pp. 60–65 (E. Senart, 1905)

sources.title: The Early History of the Deccan
sources.author: G. Yazdani

empires.historical_map_title: The Deccan Bridge — the Sātavāhana Age (c. 100 BCE–220 CE)

empires.name: Kushan Empire & The Silk Road Synthesis
empires.era_type: Trans-Eurasian Crossroads of Gandhara Art & Commerce

capitals.name: Purushapura (Peshawar)
capitals.role: Imperial primary capital; site of the towering Kanishka Stupa celebrated by Chinese pilgrims

capitals.name: Mathura
capitals.role: Southern / winter capital on the Yamuna; epicentre of indigenous Mathura sandstone sculpture

capitals.name: Kapisa / Begram
capitals.role: Summer mountain capital where the Begram treasure of Roman glass and Chinese lacquers was found

boundary_phases.description: Crossroads linking Han China, Imperial Rome, and India. Extended from Bactria and Sogdiana in Central Asia through Gandhara, Kashmir, and Punjab, down to Mathura and Varanasi.

battles.name: Kushan Expedition to Eastern India
battles.parties: Kanishka I vs. Kings of Saketa and Pataliputra
battles.summary: Kanishka conquered the Gangetic plain as far as Pataliputra, from where he took the celebrated Buddhist philosopher Ashvaghosha to his northern court.

events.title: Accession of Kanishka I; adoption of Bactrian language in Greek script for imperial coinage
Fourth Buddhist Council convened in Kashmir under Vasumitra; compilation of the Mahavibhasha
Flowering of Graeco-Buddhist Gandhara sculpture and first human representations of the Buddha

shloka_epigraph.text: φαονανφαο κανOffκε κοφανο... ινα βογοστο καραλραγγο... ογε ινα αβο ιαδο αστα καρανο βαγο λαδο φρεσταδο... οδο ματυρα οδο σιδο σαγητο οδο ζοοβο καοσαμβο οδο παταλιποτρο ॥
shloka_epigraph.translation: "The king of kings, Kanishka the Kushan... issued an edict in Greek and then put it into the Aryan language... and submitted to his will the realm of India: Champa, Saketa, Kaushambi, and Pataliputra as far as Sri Champa."
shloka_epigraph.verified_from: Nicholas Sims-Williams & Joe Cribb, Silk Road Art and Archaeology 4, 1996, pp. 75–142

sources.title: History of Civilizations of Central Asia, Vol. II
sources.author: Janos Harmatta

empires.historical_map_title: The Crossroads Empire — India under the Kushans (c. 30–375 CE)

empires.name: Gupta Empire: The Classical Golden Age
empires.era_type: Classical Zenith of Sanskrit, Science, Mathematics & Arts

capitals.name: Pataliputra
capitals.role: Imperial ancestral dynastic capital of Chandragupta I and Samudragupta

capitals.name: Ujjayini
capitals.role: Second capital and intellectual court of Chandragupta II Vikramaditya and the Navaratnas (Kalidasa, Varahamihira)

boundary_phases.description: Samudragupta violently uprooted nine kings of Aryavarta (annexed directly) and captured and liberated twelve kings of Dakshinapatha (tributary vassals down to Kanchipuram).

boundary_phases.phase: Chandragupta II Vikramaditya's Peak Empire (c. 410 CE)
boundary_phases.description: Conquest of the Western Kshatrapas in Saurashtra and Malwa gave the Guptas control of Arabian Sea maritime ports (Barygaza/Bharuch). Secured Deccan alliance via Prabhavatigupta's marriage to Vakataka King Rudrasena II.

battles.name: Eradication of the Western Kshatrapas
battles.parties: Chandragupta II Vikramaditya vs. Rudrasimha III (Saka Kshatrapa)
battles.summary: Annihilated the last Saka satrap of Gujarat and Malwa. Commemorated by issuing Gupta silver coins modeled on Kshatrapa prototypes and adopting the title 'Sakari' (Foe of the Sakas).
battles.source: Udayagiri Cave Inscriptions & Bana Bhatta's Harshacharita

battles.name: Repulsion of the Huna Invasions
battles.parties: Skandagupta vs. Kidarite / Hephthalite White Huns
battles.summary: Crown Prince Skandagupta spent a night sleeping on the bare earth before rallying the Gupta army to shatter the Huna vanguard, saving northern India from devastation.
battles.source: Bhitari Stone Pillar Inscription of Skandagupta (Ghazipur, UP)

events.title: Chandragupta I marries Licchavi Princess Kumaradevi; foundation of the Gupta Era
Chinese pilgrim Faxian visits India, noting prosperous cities without capital punishment, crime, or tolls
Birth of Aryabhata; composition of Aryabhatiya pioneering place-value zero, trigonometry, and solar system orbits
Kumaragupta I founds Nalanda Mahavihara, the great residential university

shloka_epigraph.text:
यस्य प्रज्ञानुषङ्गोचितसुखमनसः शास्त्रतत्त्वार्थभर्तुः
स्तब्धो नीचैः प्रसिद्धो बुधगुणकविभिः कीर्तिमान् राजराजः ।
सर्वपृथिवीविजयजनितोदयव्याप्तनिखिलभुवनस्य
सुचरितचरितानुबद्धावदातमतेः श्रीसमुद्रगुप्तस्य ॥
shloka_epigraph.translation: "Whose mind was filled with joy through constant communion with wisdom; who was the patron of the true spirit of the scriptures; whose famous title was King of Kings (Rajaraja); who conquered the entire earth and whose fame filled all the worlds; whose intellect was purified by virtuous conduct — Sri Samudragupta."
shloka_epigraph.citation: Allahabad Stone Pillar Inscription (Prayag Prashasti) composed by Court Poet Harishena
shloka_epigraph.verified_from: Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum (CII), Vol. III: Inscriptions of the Early Gupta Kings (J.F. Fleet, 1888, pp. 1–17)

sources.title: The Classical Age (The History and Culture of the Indian People, Vol. III)
sources.author: R.C. Majumdar (ed.)

empires.historical_map_title: India in the Gupta Golden Age (c. 320–550 CE)

empires.name: Vardhana Empire of Harsha

capitals.name: Kanyakubja (Kannauj)
capitals.role: Imperial capital (Mahodaya) on the Ganga; venue of the grand 20-nation religious assembly

capitals.name: Thanesar (Sthanishvara)
capitals.role: Ancestral seat of the Pushyabhuti dynasty in Kurukshetra

boundary_phases.description: Harsha unified the whole of northern India from Punjab to Bengal and Odisha. His southern boundary was permanently anchored along the Narmada River following his clash with Pulakeshin II.

battles.name: Battle of the Narmada
battles.parties: Harshavardhana of Kannauj vs. Pulakeshin II of Badami Chalukyas
battles.summary: Harsha marched south with vast elephant corps to subjugate the Deccan. Pulakeshin II met him on the banks of the Narmada, routing Harsha's forces and securing the title 'Parameshvara'.
battles.source: Aihole Inscription of Ravikirti (634 CE) & Xuanzang's Records

events.title: Accession of 16-year-old Harsha after the murders of his brother Rajyavardhana and brother-in-law Grahavarman
Chinese monk Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang) travels across India, residing at Harsha's court and Nalanda
Grand Kannauj Assembly celebrating Mahayana Buddhism followed by the 75-day quinquennial Prayaga charity assembly where Harsha gave away all royal treasures

shloka_epigraph.text:
अपरिमितमहिमोपनतसकलसामन्तचूडामणिमयूखवासितचरणयुगलः... परममाहेश्वरो महाराजाधिराज श्रीहर्षः ॥
स्वहस्तो मम महाराजाधिराज श्रीहर्षस्य ॥
shloka_epigraph.translation:
"Whose pair of feet is perfumed by the rays from the crest-jewels of all the feudatory kings who bowed down before his boundless majesty... The supreme devotee of Shiva (Parama-maheshvara), King of Kings, Sri Harsha.
Signed with the own hand of Sri Harsha, King of Kings."
shloka_epigraph.citation: Banskhera Copper Plate Inscription of Harsha, Year 22 (628 CE)
shloka_epigraph.verified_from: Epigraphia Indica, Vol. IV, pp. 208–211 (G. Buhler)

capitals.name: Thanjavur (Chola)
capitals.role: Chola heartland along the Kaveri delta; site of Rajaraja I's monolithic Brihadisvara granite vimana

capitals.name: Madurai (Pandya)
capitals.role: Ancient Tamil seat of the three Sangam literary academies on the Vaigai river

capitals.name: Kanchipuram (Pallava)
capitals.role: Pallava educational center and cradle of Dravidian stone architecture (Kailasanathar temple)

capitals.name: Badami / Vatapi (Chalukya)
capitals.role: Cliffside fortress capital of Pulakeshin I and II with magnificent rock-cut cave temples

boundary_phases.description: Dynamic multi-polar balance of power across peninsular India between the Badami Chalukyas in Karnataka, Pallavas in Kanchi, and the Sangam realms of the Kaveri and Vaigai basins.

battles.name: Battle of Pullalur & Sack of Vatapi
battles.summary: Led by Pallava general Paranjothi (later celebrated as saint Siruthondar), the Pallavas captured and burned Vatapi, avenging earlier defeats. Pulakeshin II died defending the ramparts.
battles.source: Kuram Copper Plates & Mahavamsa of Sri Lanka

battles.name: Battle of Venni
battles.parties: Karikala Chola vs. Confederacy of Chera, Pandya & 11 Velir Chiefs
battles.summary: Karikala shattered the allied southern coalition. The defeated Chera king Peruncheralathan committed suicide by Vadakkiruttal (fasting facing north) out of shame for receiving a wound in the back.

shloka_epigraph.text:
யாதும் ஊரே யாவரும் கேளிர்
தீதும் நன்றும் பிறர்தர வாரா
நோதலும் தணிதலும் அவற்றோ ரன்ன
சாதலும் புதுவது அன்றே... பெரியோரை வியத்தலும் இலமே
சிறியோரை இகழ்தல் அதனினும் இலமே ॥
shloka_epigraph.translation:
"Every town is our home; everyone is our kin.
Good and evil come not from others.
Pain and relief follow their own course.
Death is not a novel thing... We do not marvel at the great,
Much less do we disdain the small."
shloka_epigraph.citation: Purananuru, poem 192, composed by Kaniyan Pungundranar
shloka_epigraph.verified_from: U.V. Swaminatha Iyer Critical Sangam Edition (1894)
